item.title: Ra aims high
item.description: THE Ra High School (RHS) under-18 is the team to watch in the 2026 Vodafone Super Deans Championship as they host Ratu Kadavulevu School in their quarter-final clash at Garvey Park in Tavua this Saturday. RHS, despite being the fourth seed team from the Western Zone, beat the top seed from the Northern Zone Navatu Secondary 41-8 last Saturday at Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu.
item.content:encoded:
THE Ra High School (RHS) under-18 is the team to watch in the 2026 Vodafone Super Deans Championship as they host Ratu Kadavulevu School in their quarter-final clash at Garvey Park in Tavua this Saturday.

RHS, despite being the fourth seed team from the Western Zone, beat the top seed from the Northern Zone Navatu Secondary 41-8 last Saturday at Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu.

It was a statement performance from RHS which made the long journey to Savusavu a memorable one.

Head coach Sakiusa Dausigakoilau was clear about the team’s mindset going into the game.

“The standard of rugby required at this stage of the Deans Competition demands a whole new level of performance. We give thanks to the Almighty for what we achieved today,” he said.

RHS faces the daunting challenge of hosting defending champion Ratu Kadavulevu School.

Dausigakoilau is well aware of the task ahead and is focused on refining the team’s performance.

“As we prepare for the quarter-finals, we will return to the drawing board to identify areas for improvement and aim to come back stronger this weekend,” he explained.

The trip to Savusavu was particularly special for the coach and his players, with many experiencing their first-ever boat journey.

For Dausigakoilau, originally from Naweni, Cakaudrove in Savusavu, it was also a precious opportunity to reconnect with friends and family. Yet, when asked about his allegiance, the coach was unequivocal.

“As a teacher, we always give our best to whatever school we are sent to,” he said proudly. RHS now stands ready to face their formidable rivals in what promises to be an electrifying quarter-final showdown.

item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC will carry not only the hopes of their loyal supporters but the backing of Fiji’s entire football fraternity when they kick off their OFC Men’s Champions League 2026 campaign this weekend.

As the nation’s sole representative in Oceania’s premier club competition, the Delta Tigers have received overwhelming support from football associations and clubs across the country, who have put domestic rivalries aside in pursuit of a common goal.

From Nadi to Nasinu, Nadroga to Tailevu Naitasiri, the message has been unanimous, stand behind Rewa as they take on the region’s best.

Football officials are now urging fans to pack Churchill Park in Lautoka on Sunday and create a sea of support for Fiji’s champions against Galaxy FC.

item.title: Football fraternity unites for Rewa
item.description: SUPPORT for Rewa FC continues to grow ahead of the OFC Men’s Champions League 2026, with football associations and clubs from around the country rallying behind Fiji’s sole representative. The Nadi, Nasinu, Nadroga and Tailevu Naitasiri football associations have all extended their best wishes to the Delta Tigers as they prepare to take on Oceania’s top clubs.
item.content:encoded:
SUPPORT for Rewa FC continues to grow ahead of the OFC Men’s Champions League 2026, with football associations and clubs from around the country rallying behind Fiji’s sole representative.

The Nadi, Nasinu, Nadroga and Tailevu Naitasiri football associations have all extended their best wishes to the Delta Tigers as they prepare to take on Oceania’s top clubs.

Nadi Football Association president Mohammed Mohin said Rewa’s participation was a proud moment for Fijian football and deserved the backing of every supporter.

“Rewa has earned the opportunity to represent Fiji at the highest club level in Oceania. We wish the team every success and hope they produce performances that will make the entire country proud,” Mohin said.

Nasinu Football Club president Jagindar Singh “Rocky” echoed the sentiment, saying the tournament was an opportunity for the entire football fraternity to unite.

“Rewa is representing all of Fiji, not just one district. We wish the team every success and hope they make the nation proud,” he said.

Nadroga Football Club president Pannu Padiyachi said domestic rivalries should be set aside when a Fijian club competes on the international stage.

“Rewa is carrying the hopes of Fiji in the OFC Men’s Champions League. We wish the team all the very best and hope they make the nation proud,” he said.

Tailevu Naitasiri Football Association president Sundeep Roy also backed the Delta Tigers, saying the team would represent the entire nation when they take the field.

All four associations also called on football fans across the country to fill Churchill Park and get behind Rewa throughout the tournament, saying it was a chance for Fiji’s football community to stand together and support the nation’s representative.

Rewa opens its OFC Men’s Champions League campaign against Galaxy FC of Vanuatu at 3pm on Sunday at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

Tickets are $7 for adults, while children under 12 receive free entry.

item.title: Ranitu backs Maroons to bounce back
item.description: LAUTOKA Maroons coaching director Penioni Ranitu believes mental toughness will be the key as his side looks to bounce back from a heartbreaking opening-round defeat when they host traditional rivals Nadi in Round 2 of the Skipper Cup competition this Saturday at Churchill Park. The Maroons narrowly lost 23-24 to Nadroga in their season opener after conceding the decisive points in the closing sta
item.content:encoded:
LAUTOKA Maroons coaching director Penioni Ranitu believes mental toughness will be the key as his side looks to bounce back from a heartbreaking opening-round defeat when they host traditional rivals Nadi in Round 2 of the Skipper Cup competition this Saturday at Churchill Park.

The Maroons narrowly lost 23-24 to Nadroga in their season opener after conceding the decisive points in the closing stages, but Ranitu said the coaching staff had spent the week addressing the areas that let the team down.

“We have worked on whatever we needed to work on this week,” Ranitu said.

“We know that Nadi will come stronger after their first win against Kadavu, so we’ll try and play our own brand of rugby and counter whatever they bring on Saturday.”

Despite the rivalry between the neighbouring provinces, Ranitu said there was plenty of mutual respect between the two sides.

“We always respect Nadi. They are our neighbours, we look up to each other and we know each other well. We’ll do our best this week.”

Ranitu said the biggest lesson from the narrow defeat to Nadroga was the need to remain mentally switched on for the full 80 minutes.

“Physically we are there, but it’s about the mentality to stay focused and keep going for the whole game. We need to mentally prepare our boys, so they remain focused for the full 80 minutes and keep pushing for the win.”

He added that the team hoped to build on those improvements throughout the remainder of the Skipper Cup campaign.

Lautoka has retained much of last season’s core squad while introducing several promising youngsters into the team.

“There are a few young boys and a few new players, but most of the core squad is still here. We’ve lost Peni Matawalu as he has joined Ra Rugby, but the rest of the boys are preparing well.”

Ranitu was pleased with how the newcomers had adapted in their first outing.

item.title: Netball series raises selection dilemma
item.description: COMPETITION for places in Fiji’s squad for the Netball World Cup qualifiers intensified as players battled for selection during the first day of the invitational series on Monday. The series will help selectors identify the final 12 players who will represent Fiji at the World Cup qualifiers in Tonga, with every athlete eager to secure a place on the touring team.
item.content:encoded:
COMPETITION for places in Fiji’s squad for the Netball World Cup qualifiers intensified as players battled for selection during the first day of the invitational series on Monday.

The series will help selectors identify the final 12 players who will represent Fiji at the World Cup qualifiers in Tonga, with every athlete eager to secure a place on the touring team.

Head coach Michelle Parsons said the standard of the trial reflected the importance of the occasion, with players contesting every possession and pushing each other throughout the session.

“The girls were contesting hard for everything because obviously it’s a selection piece for them. This is who gets to make the 12 that are going to Tonga for the World Cup qualifiers.”

Parsons said the coaching staff had challenged players to execute their skills under pressure, make smart decisions and remain patient throughout the trial. She was pleased to see those areas reflected on court, while the defensive units also responded well by applying pressure and actively looking to force turnovers.

The trial also allowed the coaching staff to assess different player combinations after mixing up units during the session.

Parsons said the athletes adapted well to the changes and continued to perform despite playing alongside different teammates.

“We’ve asked the girls to look down, to think about skill execution, to make good decisions, and to be patient, and I think we saw a lot of that.”

She added that defenders were encouraged to play aggressively and disrupt the opposition rather than simply containing them, even if it meant taking calculated risks.

The strong performances throughout the trial have left selectors with a difficult task ahead of naming the final squad.

“It’s gonna be a really tough decision for the selectors.”

The final 12-player squad will represent Fiji in Tonga, where they will compete in the Netball World Cup qualifiers with a place at the next World Cup at stake.

item.title: Neighbours collide
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi Rugby vice president Jeff Tamata expects another fierce battle when his side takes on the Lautoka Maroons in Round Two of the Skipper Cup competition at Churchill Park on Saturday. Fresh from their opening-round victory over Kadavu, Tamata said preparations have remained consistent as the Jetsetters shift their focus to face one of the Skipper Cup’s traditional powerhouses.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi Rugby vice president Jeff Tamata expects another fierce battle when his side takes on the Lautoka Maroons in Round Two of the Skipper Cup competition at Churchill Park on Saturday.

Fresh from their opening-round victory over Kadavu, Tamata said preparations have remained consistent as the Jetsetters shift their focus to face one of the Skipper Cup’s traditional powerhouses.

“The preparation this week has been similar to last week. We’re taking it round by round and things have been going well,” Tamata said.

He said Nadi had escaped major injuries from the opening match but expected a much tougher challenge against a Lautoka side eager to bounce back after a narrow loss 23-24 to Nadroga last Saturday.

“Lautoka has been one of the senior teams in the Skipper Cup. They performed well last year and only lost to Nadroga through a last-minute penalty try. We know they’ll be hungry for a win in front of their home crowd.”

Tamata said discussions with the coaching staff after the Kadavu match identified several areas that needed improvement, despite the positive start to the campaign.

“The first game is always tough. We’ve gotten through that hurdle, but there are still a lot of things we need to address before Saturday.”

While the final squad is yet to be named, Tamata said Nadi has full confidence in its player development system and depth, with more young talent expected to feature after eight debutants impressed in the opening round against Kadavu last Saturday.

Nadi will face Lautoka this Saturday at 3pm at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

· Naitasiri v Kadavu at Ratu Cakobau Park

item.title: Fijiana xv chase historic honour
item.description: THE warm smiles shared between Fijiana captain Kolora Lomani and Springbok Women skipper Libbe Janse van Rensburg at the Fiji Museum in Suva yesterday will soon give way to fierce rivalry when they face off this Saturday at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva. item.content:encoded:
THE warm smiles shared between Fijiana captain Kolora Lomani and Springbok Women skipper Libbe Janse van Rensburg at the Fiji Museum in Suva yesterday will soon give way to fierce rivalry when they face off this Saturday at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva.

Standing alongside the newly unveiled Ubuntu-Bula Trophy, the two captains officially launched what promises to become a lasting emblem of the burgeoning rivalry between Fiji and South Africa in women’s rugby.

For the first time, the Fijiana XV and the Springbok Women will contest a trophy crafted exclusively for a Test, adding fresh significance to Saturday’s showdown at the HFC Bank National Stadium.

More than just silverware, the Ubuntu-Bula Trophy symbolises the shared values of two proud rugby nations.

Inspired by the South African philosophy of Ubuntu—”I am because we are”—it represents unity, compassion, teamwork, respect, fair play, and humility.

Paired with Fiji’s beloved greeting, Bula, which wishes life, health, and happiness, the trophy celebrates the friendship between the two countries while honouring the fierce yet respectful battles on the pitch.

Lomani hailed the unveiling as a historic moment for Fijian rugby.

“We hadn’t expected a trophy, so seeing it today was truly special—not just for the women’s team but for all of Fiji,” she said.

“We haven’t played South Africa in a long time, so this trophy adds an exciting new chapter and inspires young talents aiming to wear the national colours.”

Janse van Rensburg echoed the enthusiasm, calling the trophy a highlight of her day and a testament to the rising profile of women’s rugby in both nations.

When the final whistle sounds at the national stadium this Saturday, history will be made as one nation becomes the inaugural holder of the Ubuntu-Bula Trophy, while a new and meaningful chapter is added to one of women’s rugby’s emerging international rivalries.

item.title: Cuvu count on stars
item.description: CUVU College has adopted a new coaching approach this season, bringing in former Nadroga provincial and national representatives to strengthen its Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Deans campaign. The move has paid dividends, with the Western Zone champions now preparing for their Under-18 quarterfinal clash against Nasinu Secondary School at Garvey Park in Tavua this Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
CUVU College has adopted a new coaching approach this season, bringing in former Nadroga provincial and national representatives to strengthen its Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Deans campaign.

The move has paid dividends, with the Western Zone champions now preparing for their Under-18 quarterfinal clash against Nasinu Secondary School at Garvey Park in Tavua this Saturday.

Head coach Luke Salaba said the decision to include experienced former players in the coaching panel had transformed the team’s performance and mindset.

“In previous seasons, when only teachers coached the team, we would often fall short at the elimination or quarterfinal stage.

“This year we decided to do things differently by bringing in experts to work with the players in different areas of the game, including the forwards and backline,” Salaba said.

Salaba said the impact had been evident throughout the season.

“We have seen a change in the players’ attitude and a different approach to the game. The experience these former players bring has been invaluable.”

Former Nadroga representatives Jiuta Wainiqolo, Setefano Somoca and Emosi Vucago are among those assisting the coaching staff.

Cuvu showcased their exciting brand of rugby in last week’s quarterfinal victory over St John’s College, with their pace, physicality and structured play proving too much for their opponents.

The side will now be aiming to carry that momentum into Saturday’s knockout clash as they continue their quest for Deans glory.
